rules.claim: The documents API is routed to UnifiedSearchViewSet, whose inherited DocumentViewSet contains a notes(request, pk=None) handler; that handler loads the addressed document by pk before method dispatch.
The caller principal used by the notes handler is request.user, assigned to currentUser.
The addressed document is selected by pk and loaded as doc; owner is selected with the document and the same doc is passed to the permission check.
Before GET dispatch, the handler invokes has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, "view_document", doc) and returns HTTP 403 when that check is false.
For GET, after the upstream view_document check, the handler serializes the addressed document and returns its notes representation.

The documents API is routed to UnifiedSearchViewSet, whose inherited DocumentViewSet contains a notes(request, pk=None) handler; that handler loads the addressed document by pk before method dispatch.
The caller principal used by the notes handler is request.user, assigned to currentUser.
The addressed document is selected by pk and loaded as doc; the same doc is passed to both the initial and POST-specific permission checks and to Note.objects.create(document=doc,...).
Before POST dispatch, the handler invokes has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, "view_document", doc) and returns HTTP 403 when that check is false.
For POST, after the initial view_document check, the handler invokes has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, "change_document", doc) and returns HTTP 403 when that check is false.
For POST, after the change_document check, Note.objects.create creates a Note attached to the addressed doc, using request data and currentUser.
The GET scenario uses the view_document owner-aware check on the addressed doc before returning that document's notes.
The POST scenario uses an initial view_document check and then a change_document owner-aware check on the addressed doc before creating a note attached to that doc.
